content.title: About
content.content: Peanuts are a legume whose seeds are commonly called nuts. Roasted unsalted peanuts have a distinctive aroma, crunchy texture, and a mildly sweet flavor. They are eaten raw, roasted, and used in cooking, confectionery, sauces, and spreads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanuts belong to the legume family, not true nuts, although they are used like nuts in cuisine.
They originated in South America and were domesticated more than 3,500 years ago.
Peanut plants produce flowers that bend down to the ground, where they are fertilized and develop pods – the so‑called "groundnuts."
The United States produces over 30 % of the world’s peanuts, making it the largest producer.
Peanuts are used to make peanut butter, pastes, flour, and even peanut oil.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Peanuts contain about 25 % protein, providing a valuable plant‑based protein source.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: They are high in monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Peanuts provide niacin, thiamine, and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They supply magnesium, phosphorus, potassium, and iron, aiding muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Peanuts contain resveratrol and phenolic compounds that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are one of the most common food allergens and can cause severe reactions.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Because of their fat content, peanuts are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Aflatoxins
items.content: Improper storage can lead to mold growth that produces aflatoxins; keep peanuts dry to avoid contamination.

items.title: Omega‑6 fatty acids
items.content: A high omega‑6 to omega‑3 ratio may promote inflammation if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peanuts can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, yogurts, cereals, baked goods, sauces, and spreads. They are also processed into peanut butter and flour. Roasted unsalted peanuts are a versatile, health‑friendly option.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store peanuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any nuts that smell rancid.
